public.title: JSON.stringify
public.description: Serialize a JSON value to compact JSON text, matching JSON.stringify without replacer or indentation. Preserve Object.keys order for object properties and array order. Escape string contents correctly, including quotes, backslashes and control characters. Only the bounded JSON domain is supported; undefined, functions, cycles and special objects are excluded. This is an instructional implementation exercise; fixtures do not enforce a ban on native stringify. Supported inputs are dense JSON values only: at most 100 total nodes, nesting depth at most 6, each string at most 80 UTF-16 code units, and integers from -1000 through 1000 unless narrower bounds are given. Unless the adapter explicitly defines path keys or another key format, object keys are nonempty ASCII letters without dots. All keys exclude prototype-related names. Inputs are valid; no validation is requested. Array order matters, object key order does not. Return a JSON value; no browser or third-party library is available. The complete serialized argument array is limited to 2048 UTF-8 bytes, counting JSON escaping. These whole-input limits also apply to descriptors, operations and nested values.
hints: Track the distinctions and boundary rules in the statement before coding.
Recursively serialize values and quote strings using the platform string-escaping primitive.

referenceSolutions.javascript:
export function solve(value) {
  const quote = (s) => JSON.stringify(s);
  const encode = (v) =>
    v === null
      ? "null"
      : typeof v === "string"
        ? quote(v)
        : typeof v === "number" || typeof v === "boolean"
          ? String(v)
          : Array.isArray(v)
            ? "[" + v.map(encode).join(",") + "]"
            : "{" +
              Object.keys(v)
                .map((k) => quote(k) + ":" + encode(v[k]))
                .join(",") +
              "}";
  return encode(value);
}

export function solve(value: any): any {
  const quote = (s: string): string => JSON.stringify(s);
  const encode = (v: any): string =>
    v === null
      ? "null"
      : typeof v === "string"
        ? quote(v)
        : typeof v === "number" || typeof v === "boolean"
          ? String(v)
          : Array.isArray(v)
            ? "[" + v.map(encode).join(",") + "]"
            : "{" +
              Object.keys(v)
                .map((k) => quote(k) + ":" + encode(v[k]))
                .join(",") +
              "}";
  return encode(value);
}

explanation: Recursively serialize values and quote strings using the platform string-escaping primitive. O(encoded size) time and space; this variant isolates JSON structure rather than reimplementing all string escapes.
